edges.description: Reduced or absent nesprin-1 impairs assembly and function of the LINC complex at the nuclear envelope.

Intellectual disability in the childhood-onset multisystem presentation. Wired from the primary genetic lesion rather than from cerebellar degeneration because that presentation is not the cerebellar syndrome this pathograph otherwise models.
Muscle weakness and wasting in the childhood-onset multisystem presentation.
Decreased fetal movements in the arthrogryposis presentation. The intermediates between nesprin-1 loss and reduced fetal movement are not established.
Severe neonatal hypotonia in the arthrogryposis presentation.
Multiple congenital joint contractures at the severe end of the SYNE1 deficiency spectrum.
Clubfoot among the congenital contractures of the arthrogryposis presentation.
Scoliosis as a non-neurological feature of the extracerebellar SYNE1 phenotype. Attributed to the primary lesion because no cerebellar mechanism accounts for it.
Pes cavus as a non-neurological feature of the extracerebellar SYNE1 phenotype.
Respiratory dysfunction in severely affected non-founder patients.
Strabismus is reported in SYNE1 ataxia but is not a cerebellar sign, so it is attributed to the primary lesion rather than routed through cerebellar degeneration.
Disrupted nuclear-cytoskeletal coupling in cerebellar neurons leads to cerebellar degeneration manifesting as diffuse cerebellar atrophy.
The broader SYNE1 deficiency spectrum includes upper motor neuron signs beyond the pure cerebellar phenotype.
Cerebellar-plus SYNE1 deficiency can include lower motor neuron involvement outside the classic pure cerebellar presentation.
Spasticity as a component sign of the upper motor neuron arm.
Hyperreflexia as a component sign of the upper motor neuron arm.
Brisk lower-extremity reflexes, the upper motor neuron sign actually observed in the otherwise pure-cerebellar Beauce founder cohort.
Extensor plantar response as a component sign of the upper motor neuron arm.
Amyotrophy as a component sign of the lower motor neuron arm.
Reduced deep tendon reflexes as a component sign of the lower motor neuron arm.
Fasciculations as a component sign of the lower motor neuron arm.
Diffuse cerebellar atrophy is the imaging correlate of the cerebellar neurodegenerative process.
Cerebellar degeneration produces the progressive cerebellar ataxia syndrome.
Cerebellar degeneration manifests clinically as gait ataxia.
Cerebellar degeneration impairs appendicular coordination, producing limb ataxia.
Cerebellar degeneration causes the dysarthria component of the syndrome.
Cerebellar degeneration causes dysmetria as part of the pure cerebellar syndrome.
Cerebellar degeneration affects ocular motor control, including smooth pursuit.
Cerebellar ocular motor involvement includes slow saccadic eye movements.
Cerebellar ocular motor involvement includes gaze-evoked nystagmus.
Cerebellar involvement can extend to cerebellar cognitive and affective syndrome.
Attentional deficit as a specific domain of the cerebellar cognitive and affective syndrome.
Square-wave jerks as part of the cerebellar ocular motor disturbance.
Broken-up (saccadic) smooth pursuit as part of the cerebellar ocular motor disturbance.
Swallowing difficulty accompanying the bulbar/cerebellar motor speech disturbance, flagged by GeneReviews for ongoing surveillance.

nodes.description: Nesprin-1 participates in the LINC complex spanning the nuclear envelope (SUN-KASH bridging), physically connecting the cytoskeleton to nuclear components and mediating nuclear positioning, cell migration, and mechanotransduction. Loss of nesprin-1 disrupts this coupling. The LINC complex is essential to nervous-system development, and LINC-gene mutations are implicated in neurodegenerative disease.

evidence.snippet: The linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) complex, which spans the nuclear envelope, physically connects nuclear components to the cytoskeleton and plays a pivotal role in various cellular processes, including nuclear positioning, cell migration, and chromosomal configuration.

nodes.description: ARCA1 is caused by biallelic SYNE1 variants, most commonly truncating loss-of- function alleles, that reduce or abolish nesprin-1. This establishes the primary molecular lesion.
